people.name: Agnes Doyle
people.role: a dentist with rooms on the third floor

secret.label: Forged identity
secret.description: Doyle is not the person the papers say. Nothing about the evening is hidden; the lie is all in the paperwork.

motive.description: wanted the victim out of a lease

secret.label: Fencing stolen goods
secret.description: Vitale hands a parcel of stolen goods to a man at Dolan’s from 8:30 PM.

secret.label: Gambling debt
secret.description: Crowninshield slips off to Dolan’s from 7:30 PM to 8:00 PM to settle with a bookmaker.

motive.description: blamed the victim for a ruin

secret.label: Murder
secret.description: Corrigan is at the drying yard from 8:30 PM, alone with Vogel when it happens at 8:30 PM.

coverSecret.label: Blackmailing the victim
coverSecret.description: Corrigan meets the victim alone at the brownstone from 7:30 PM and asks for money.

people.name: Lurline Bledsoe
people.role: a widow with rooms on the avenue
people.relationshipToVictim: the victim’s neighbour across the airshaft

secret.label: A child boarded out
secret.description: Bledsoe goes to the parlour from 8:30 PM to see a child nobody is supposed to know about.

people.name: Ernst Schilling
people.relationshipToVictim: a childhood friend of the victim’s from the same block

secret.label: Gambling debt
secret.description: Schilling slips off to Dolan’s from 8:30 PM to 9:00 PM to settle with a bookmaker.

Vogel was found at the drying yard. The tap was left running and the basin had overflowed a clean ring onto the boards. The last edition came off the truck at 8:30 PM, and a paper from that run is here with the ink still wet.
The coroner puts death between 7:00 PM and 8:30 PM — two hours of nothing useful. A single narrow puncture under the ribs. Very little blood outside the body.
An ice pick is gone from Dolan’s. The block is out and half melted and the pick that belongs with it is gone.
Moretti puts Vogel at the parlour while the singing was still going on, which was 8:00 PM, and alive enough to argue about the weather.
Doyle was at the parlour at 8:30 PM and heard a struggle and something going over from the direction of the drying yard, as the last edition was coming up.
Crowninshield was at the parlour at 8:30 PM and heard a struggle and something going over from the direction of the drying yard, as the last edition was coming up.
Moretti was at the parlour at 8:30 PM and heard a struggle and something going over from the direction of the drying yard, as the last edition was coming up.
Zeldin came round at 8:00 PM and had Crowninshield at Dolan’s.
Zeldin came round at 8:00 PM and had Corrigan at Dolan’s.
Zeldin came round at 9:30 PM and had Doyle at the parlour.
Found at the brownstone: A lease assignment made out in Doyle’s name, waiting only on Vogel’s signature.
Wehrle says Vogel told Doyle the lease would go to somebody else at the quarter day.
Found at the brownstone: A clipping about the failure of Crowninshield’s business, with Vogel’s name underlined twice in pencil.
Vitale says Crowninshield said Vogel had taken everything and would be made to feel it.
Found at the Bijou: Three letters in Vogel’s hand to a woman Corrigan is engaged to, kept in a drawer, the last one opened.
Wehrle says Corrigan told Vogel to keep away, loud enough to turn heads.
Found at the brownstone: A promissory note for $4,000 signed by Schilling, endorsed to Vogel, three months past due.
Moretti says Vogel told Schilling that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
Corrigan hired us, and wants it known that Doyle wanted the victim out of a lease, and would rather we started there.
Rosenbaum on Doyle: Doyle’s registration card gives an address on a street that does not exist.
Zeldin on Doyle: Two signatures of Doyle’s, a month apart, are in different hands.
Crowninshield on Doyle: Doyle answers to the name a half-second late, every time.
A union card in Doyle’s coat lining carries a different surname and a 1919 date.
A steamship ticket stub among Doyle’s things, in the name of a man who died at Belleau Wood.
The name Doyle was born with turns up on a desertion warrant from 1918. Doyle has been hiding from the Army for eleven years and from nobody else.
The papers are forged and the reason is plain: Doyle was put out of the country once already and does not mean to be put out twice.
Wehrle on Vitale: Vitale was carrying a parcel into Dolan’s and came out without it.
Doyle on Vitale: There is a man who meets people at Dolan’s and nobody will say his name out loud.
Moretti on Vitale: Vitale has been selling things that were never Vitale’s to sell.
Wrapping paper and a cut string at Dolan’s, and the shop it came from closed two years ago.
A pawn ticket at Dolan’s in a name that does not exist, made out at the hour in question.
The receiver at Dolan’s would rather talk than be held: Vitale was there from 8:30 PM handing over a parcel of somebody else’s silver, which is a charge Vitale will take over this one.
The goods turn up, tagged and dated, and the tag puts Vitale at Dolan’s from 8:30 PM with both hands full.
Zeldin on Crowninshield: Crowninshield was asking around for a hundred dollars in a hurry earlier in the week.
Vitale on Crowninshield: A man nobody knew was waiting for Crowninshield at Dolan’s and would not give a name.
Schilling on Crowninshield: Crowninshield goes very quiet when the racing wire is mentioned.
Betting slips at Dolan’s in Crowninshield’s pocketbook, all of them losers, all of them this month.
A book of markers at Dolan’s with Crowninshield’s initials against four of them.
The bookmaker’s runner is found and will say it: Crowninshield was at Dolan’s from 7:30 PM to 8:00 PM paying off eleven hundred dollars, a dollar at a time, and went nowhere near the killing.
The book at Dolan’s has the payment entered against Crowninshield’s name and the time beside it, from 7:30 PM to 8:00 PM, in the clerk’s own hand.
Doyle on Bledsoe: Bledsoe sends money out of every pay envelope and cannot say where it goes.
Moretti on Bledsoe: A woman at the parlour asked for Bledsoe by a name Bledsoe has not used in years.
Wehrle on Bledsoe: Bledsoe keeps a photograph and will not be asked about it twice.
A board-and-keep receipt at the parlour, monthly, eight years of them.
A child’s shoe at the parlour, and nobody at the parlour has any children.
The woman who keeps the child says it straight out: Bledsoe was at the parlour from 8:30 PM, the same as every week, and left with the same face as always.
The parish register at the parlour has the christening in it, and the board money receipted through the evening in question.
Crowninshield on Schilling: Schilling was asking around for a hundred dollars in a hurry earlier in the week.
Rosenbaum on Schilling: A man nobody knew was waiting for Schilling at Dolan’s and would not give a name.
Zeldin on Schilling: Schilling goes very quiet when the racing wire is mentioned.
Betting slips at Dolan’s in Schilling’s pocketbook, all of them losers, all of them this month.
A book of markers at Dolan’s with Schilling’s initials against four of them.
The bookmaker’s runner is found and will say it: Schilling was at Dolan’s from 8:30 PM to 9:00 PM paying off eleven hundred dollars, a dollar at a time, and went nowhere near the killing.
The book at Dolan’s has the payment entered against Schilling’s name and the time beside it, from 8:30 PM to 9:00 PM, in the clerk’s own hand.
